, the 3D structure of the airways is important for the development of the lung, and for the function of the lung, but that the exact relationship between 3D airway structure and pulmonary function is not known.
, the 3D structure of the airways and pulmonary parenchyma is a determinant of the mechanical behavior and function of the lung.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the three-dimensional structure of the airway tree is related to the mechanical properties of the lung, and that the airway tree structure can be measured noninvasively.
the three-dimensional architecture of the airways is important for understanding the pathophysiology of lung disease, and for the design of devices that interact with the lung.
we developed a novel approach to quantify the airway tree architecture in 3D, and used the information to study the relationship between airway tree architecture, pulmonary function and disease.

the airway tree architecture is a key determinant of pulmonary function.
the three-dimensional architecture of the human airway tree, as determined by CT, is associated with pulmonary function.
